fixed.explanation: validate_metadata calls array_equivalent with dtype_equal=True even when the stored and new categories have different dtypes (int vs float). This skips the dtype check and reaches the Cython routine with mismatched buffers. Adding an explicit dtype comparison makes differing dtypes count as different categories, so the intended ValueError is raised.

query.intent: When appending to a PyTables table-format store, the code validates that new categorical categories match the stored ones (in the categorical/Categorical column handling in pandas/io/pytables.py, e.g. validate_col / update_info / _maybe_convert / metadata comparison). It compares categories arrays of different dtypes with a Cython/hashtable-based routine (e.g. array_equivalent or Index.equals/isin) that raises a buffer dtype mismatch instead of returning False, so the intended "cannot append categories differ" ValueError is not raised.
query.symptom: Appending a categorical column with float categories to a table-format HDFStore key holding integer categories raises "ValueError: Buffer dtype mismatch, expected 'double' but got 'long'" instead of the intended different-categories ValueError.
